subject.title: [Bug]: In msteams channel messages, OpenClaw can't access inbound attachments

question: Should Microsoft Teams non-personal Graph media fallback stay default-off behind a new `channels.msteams.graphMediaFallback` option, or should OpenClaw automatically attempt Graph lookup whenever Bot Framework delivered HTML but no media was extracted?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the default affects existing deployments through extra Graph reads, permission expectations, diagnostics, and the prior mention-only false-positive protection.

options.title: Default-off opt-in fallback
options.body: Adopt a config-gated fallback so existing installs keep current behavior unless operators explicitly enable extra Graph media reads.

options.title: Automatic non-personal fallback
options.body: Relax the gate for all non-personal HTML activities with no media, accepting extra Graph traffic to make attachments work without new config.

options.title: Combine both fix candidates
options.body: Ask one branch to cover channel aadGroupId/reply URL fixes and the group-chat fallback gate so the compatibility story lands once.

recommendation.title: Default-off opt-in fallback
recommendation.body: Adopt a config-gated fallback so existing installs keep current behavior unless operators explicitly enable extra Graph media reads.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-history signal across the msteams media and channel-delivery files, while the remaining blocker is a compatibility/default decision.
